question: Does reparameterizing LM polish's omega onto the polhode basis improve Band A yield and in-basin convergence speed vs the s059k baseline?
hypothesis: Polhode-basis omega reparameterization lifts Band A yield and speeds in-basin convergence (per the s063b curvature ratio).
narrative_md: Reparameterizing LM polish's omega onto the polhode basis (Gram-Schmidt from grad 2T and grad L^2, per s063b) lifts seed-89 Band A yield from 4/50 to 5/50 unique clusters. The new cluster id=125 lands the truth basin (q0_err 0.86 deg, rho 0.176) from a representative s059k's standard polish missed. In-basin smoke convergence is 21-27x faster (3-4 s vs 85 s). The polhode basis improves IN-basin convergence but does not widen the basin -- multi-mag-start and grid densification remain necessary. Gate3 yield is genuine (truth not in top-50); but Gate1/Gate2 read truth/perturbed-truth (oracle-leak).
